solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Permit given to fine land yet to be cultivated

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
to permit is to allow

explanation.surface: A farmer is granted leave to keep some ground unploughed for now.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallow describes farmland ploughed but left unsown, so here it stands for ground awaiting cultivation.

clue.text: A state benefit reportedly dispatched to juvenile

parts.note: the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit paid by the state

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: dispatched means sent

explanation.surface: Welfare payments are being sent to a young person.
explanation.definitionFit: A juvenile is a young person, and an adolescent is a teenager in that same youthful stage.

clue.text: Delays experienced by convicts

definitions.meaning: ... are intervals of delay, as in time ...

explanation.surface: Prisoners are held up in their release.
explanation.definitionFit: Lags means both hold-ups in time and, in British slang, prisoners serving sentences.

clue.text: An urge to stray wasn't ruled out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of the preceding words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone insists a desire to roam was never actually forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruled out' reads as a phrase meaning excluded, but 'out' alone is the anagram signal for WASNT RULED.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanderlust is a strong desire to travel and roam, an urge to stray far from home.

clue.text: Increases support for campaign for exercises

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece sits under the first, holding it up as support

parts.note: a push is a concerted campaign or effort
ups as a noun means increases, as in ups and downs

explanation.surface: Higher funding props up a fitness campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Push-ups are floor exercises raising the body by straightening the arms; the plural matches.

clue.text: Measure taken to back favourites

indicators.note: to back suggests going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A gambler takes action to put money on the favourites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as betting on the favourites, but it signals a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a measure taken towards some end, as in taking steps to fix a problem.

clue.text: Radio star is torn, in other words

indicators.note: in other words hints that the same letters are recast into different words

explanation.surface: A broadcasting celebrity is pulled two ways, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A transistor was the everyday name for a small portable radio set built from such components.

clue.text: Farmer longing to grab hold of old master

indicators.note: to grab hold of says the first word clutches the other pieces within it

parts.note: a yen is a longing
MA is Master of Arts, a master's degree

explanation.surface: A farmer eager to seize the property of a former landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeoman was historically a man farming his own small holding of land.

clue.text: Grown up with age, note, can be corrupt

parts.note: an adult is a grown-up
an era is an age
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Becoming an adult and older brings moral decay, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' is a verb here, as in spoiling food by adding impurities.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate is to debase or spoil something by mixing in inferior matter.

clue.text: Union bastion holds scope for redevelopment

indicators.note: for redevelopment suggests the letters are rebuilt into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A trade union stronghold has room to be rebuilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed shop is a workplace where union membership is compulsory, a stronghold of trade union power.

clue.text: The average minor perhaps has no one

indicators.note: perhaps shows the letters are only a possible arrangement, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A typical youngster is said to be without any company.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I out of MINOR, as 'has no one' says, and rearrange the remaining MNOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The norm is the usual or average standard of a group.

clue.text: Ship's steward has a way of attracting attention

indicators.note: has indicates the letters are held within the run of words

explanation.surface: A cruise attendant has a method for catching passengers' eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the hissed interjection used to quietly catch somebody's notice.

clue.text: Subject leaves the car in areas offering amusements

parts.note: a theme is a subject
to park is to leave a car standing

explanation.surface: A topic of conversation: abandoning the car at fairground sites.
explanation.definitionFit: Theme parks are large grounds offering rides and entertainment, plural to match areas.

clue.text: Political affiliation of a landlord chasing 50% of rent

indicators.note: chasing places the following piece behind the preceding one
50% of asks for the first half of the word

parts.note: a publican is the landlord of a pub, in British usage

explanation.surface: The politics of a property owner after half the rent money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landlord' suggests property letting, but in Britain it is also the keeper of a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Republican names a political allegiance, whether to a US party or to anti-monarchy views.

clue.text: Nonsense talked about having less hair and flair

parts.note: balder means having less hair
dash means flair or style

explanation.surface: Gossip about a man's thinning hair and lack of style is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is senseless talk or writing, a synonym for twaddle.

clue.text: Combine fixing a game with Malta

indicators.note: fixing suggests tampering with the letters to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Match-fixing allegations involving the Maltese team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixing' reads as rigging a match but is the anagram signal for A GAME MALTA; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To amalgamate is to merge or join together into a single whole.

clue.text: Feel remorse, accepting regular income

indicators.note: accepting has the first word take the second inside it

parts.note: to rue is to feel remorse
even means regular or steady

explanation.surface: Someone regrets taking a steady salary.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is income, especially money coming in to a business or state.

clue.text: Plain gold affixed to denture

indicators.note: affixed to attaches the piece at the end of the other

parts.note: a plate is a set of false teeth on a base
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A dentist bonds gold to a set of false teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective describing the gold but is a noun for flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an elevated plain, a level stretch of high ground.

clue.text: Objecting to China being full of noise

indicators.note: being full of puts the second piece inside the first

parts.note: Ming is the Chinese dynasty famous for its porcelain
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the porcelain rattles noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is Ming, the dynasty whose name is used for its porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Minding means objecting, as in do you mind?, taking exception to something.

clue.text: Shrewd setter gets upset with one's early start

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: one is I, so one's gives I followed by S

indicators.note: start asks for the first letter

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler grows angry yet stays sharp from the off.
explanation.definitionFit: Streetwise means shrewd and savvy about the ways of urban life.

clue.text: Meagre lines finally accepted by extra

indicators.note: accepted by places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: spare means extra

indicators.note: finally asks for the final letter

explanation.surface: A poet's lines are taken up, though few.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered or scanty, close to meagre.

clue.text: Boasts of going topless in the tabloids

indicators.note: going topless removes the top, or first, letter of the word

parts.note: brags means boasts

explanation.surface: Lurid stories of a topless outing appear in the gossip press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' suggests a tabloid scandal, but it signals dropping the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rags is slang for low-quality newspapers, the tabloids in particular.

clue.text: The strain of non-drinkers accepting ruin, oddly

indicators.note: accepting has the first piece take the other inside it

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, an association of non-drinkers

indicators.note: oddly asks for the odd-numbered letters

explanation.surface: Abstainers suffer the stress of drink having wrecked lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' suggests stress but means a melody here.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a passage of music, and an aria is a solo song in opera.

clue.text: Personal assistant's strange idea to abscond

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are made unusual by rearranging

parts.note: to decamp is to depart suddenly or abscond

explanation.surface: A secretary has an odd notion of running off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' turns IDEA into AIDE; the 's is a link meaning has.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide-de-camp is an officer acting as personal assistant to a senior commander.

clue.text: Long to be expelled by teachers

indicators.note: expelled by says the letters come out of the following word

explanation.surface: Pupils yearn to be thrown out by the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective but is a verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to long or yearn for it.

clue.text: Reminded when recovered from illness, having lost heart

indicators.note: having lost heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: cured means recovered from illness

explanation.surface: A patient got better but was dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost heart' reads as discouraged, but it removes the middle letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Cued means prompted or given a signal, as an actor is reminded of a line.

clue.text: Rattle the workers and extend a greeting

parts.note: to rattle is to shake
hands are workers, as in farm hands

explanation.surface: A boss unsettles staff yet offers a friendly welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake hands is the customary gesture when greeting someone.

clue.text: Hospital boundaries?

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
edges are boundaries

explanation.surface: A query about the perimeter of a medical site.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the whole clue doubles as a loose description: shrubbery boundaries might surround a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedges are rows of shrubs forming boundaries between fields or gardens.
